correctedCritiques.con-suffering-counterevidence-not-defeat: Strongest feature: Edwards candidly acknowledges suffering as the strongest counterevidence, distinguishes substantial evidential pressure from a decisive defeater, and invokes Christian considerations instead of minimizing the objection’s seriousness. Principal limitation: His compressed references to cosmic disorder, afterlife, theodicies, and divine participation establish compatibility without demonstrating how those considerations probabilistically explain particular apparently gratuitous horrors. Live burden: Edwards must connect every consideration to suffering’s distribution and severity, explaining why an omnipotent, perfectly loving deity would permit such cases and why compensating goods provide morally sufficient justification. Locked score: The very-strong band reflects exceptional relevance, calibration, explicit concession, and direct engagement, while preserving an evidential limitation because the responses receive names more fully than defended probability-changing mechanisms.
correctedCritiques.pro-creator-evidence-classical-god-gap: Strongest feature: Woodford conditionally grants positive arguments and identifies the inferential distance between establishing a creator and establishing the omnipotent, perfectly loving deity targeted by the motion. Principal limitation: A cumulative case might attribute characteristics jointly rather than require a design or moral argument to establish the classical conception, so the identity gap does not defeat Edwards’s combined evidence. Live burden: Woodford must establish that apparently gratuitous suffering remains improbable under the cumulative classical hypothesis, while Edwards must demonstrate how his arguments identify the attributes and reconcile them with evil. Locked score: The very-strong band reflects conditional reasoning, stable scope, responsiveness, and direct contact with central claims, moderated because gratuitousness and cumulative identification require comparative defense.
